- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.3) — raise forecast lows.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak.
- Lagged price movements often underestimated — adjust forecast to align with 2–3 prior days’ true trend.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overreact to short-term sentiment — dampen momentum-driven spikes.
- If sentiment is rising but price is flat or falling, reduce forecast slope to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
